# TDPdf v1.23.0.0

You can now see, control and switch off what TDPdf reports — and it keeps reporting when you are offline instead of quietly losing it.

## Telemetry you can actually turn off

**Settings → Privacy → "Send anonymous usage and crash reports."** On by default, and it takes effect the moment you untick it.

Reporting now needs two separate things: your consent, *and* a destination configured by whoever deployed TDPdf. Either one alone sends nothing. The setting tells you which of those two states your machine is in, rather than leaving you to guess whether you have just switched off something that was never on.

There is also a new **[PRIVACY.md](../../blob/main/PRIVACY.md)** in the repository listing exactly what is collected and what never is. Two things in it are worth knowing without having to go and read it: reports carry your **machine name**, and they carry a **session identifier** that is generated fresh every time TDPdf starts and is never written to disk, so it cannot link one run to another.

Your documents are not involved. No file contents, no file names, no file paths — and stack traces have paths stripped out before they are sent.

## Reports no longer vanish when you are offline

Two problems, both fixed.

If TDPdf could not reach the server, the report was simply dropped. It is now queued on your machine and sent when you reconnect. On a laptop that is not an edge case — being offline, on hotel wifi, or off the VPN is normal, and it meant the people who travel most were the least represented in the data.

And if a crash killed the application outright, the crash report died with it, still in memory. Crash reports are now written to disk *as they happen* and sent at the next launch. That is not theoretical: some of the crashes fixed in 1.22.1.0 left no trace at all, and were only found by noticing the gap.

Both queues live under your own user profile, hold only the sanitised data described above, and are safe to delete at any time.

## For administrators

**The telemetry destination is now delivered as managed policy rather than compiled into the executable.** Rotating the key becomes a policy push instead of rebuilding, re-signing and redeploying to every device — which is the honest reason the previous key was never rotated. See *Telemetry policy profile* in `docs/intune-distribution.md`.

The embedded key stays as a deprecated fallback so machines that have not yet received the policy keep reporting.

**Nothing changes on the Azure side.** Application Insights keeps every alert rule and query it has; this adds a second destination rather than replacing the first. And **the new path is inert until you configure it** — with no policy key present, behaviour is identical to 1.22.1.0.

The Intune detection rule now requires 1.23.0.0, so managed machines will pick this up on the next evaluation. Assignments are unaffected.

## Verifying this download

The executable is signed by *The Doodle Project Code Signing*, a private certificate. On managed machines that trust it, the signature validates. On a machine that does not, Windows will still warn on first run. Use `SHA256SUMS.txt` to confirm the download independently.
